properties.decision: Where fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server and fact:correction-stranded-server-is-recoverable-without-a-reconnect disagree, THE CORRECTION STANDS: a session stranded by the deleted-inode spawn failure IS recoverable in place, by starting a replacement daemon by hand from the on-disk path. The original node's remaining claims — the spawn failure itself, its cause in current_exe() resolving a deleted inode, and its misleading 'check the server log' advice — are unaffected and still hold.
properties.name: The recoverability clause is withdrawn; the rest of the stranded-server defect stands
properties.rationale: Recorded because detect_defects reported the CONTRADICTS edge as an unresolved contradiction, and it was right to: two facts about the same failure disagreed, and nothing said which a reader should act on. Left alone, the next stranded session finds both and has no way to choose — which is worse than either claim alone, because the expensive answer ('unrecoverable, restart the session') is the one written with more authority. WHY THE CORRECTION WINS ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ON RECENCY: it was established by execution on 2026-08-08 — the failure was hit, the recovery run, and a dozen subsequent tool calls succeeded in the same session with no reconnect. The original clause was inherited from a session handoff and reasoned from the spawn path, never tested; the node's own evidence field says the diagnosis was 'recorded ... as worth filing and still unfiled'. A measured claim beats a reasoned one about the same mechanism. THE DISTINCTION THAT MAKES BOTH NODES TRUE ONCE THIS IS APPLIED: the dead inode blocks the client from CREATING a daemon, not from FINDING one. Attaching is a separate act, and any daemon started by any means satisfies the lookup. So the original is right about spawn and wrong about the session. NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the original node's statement is left intact rather than edited. Its wrong clause is now answered on the record instead of erased, which keeps visible that reflow2's own graph carried a confident untested claim for a day — the same failure class the design keeps finding elsewhere, and worth being able to point at.
